children: said Friday it signed contracts worth €1.2B with TransPennine Express for the supply and long-term maintenance of a new fleet of battery-electric trains in the U.K., supporting the ongoing decarbonization of one of Britain's most important rail corridors.
The agreements combine a rolling stock contract worth €930M for 29 five-car battery-electric Adessia Stream trains to be built at Alstom's
Litchurch Lane factory in Derby, with maintenance contracts valued at around €230M.
The order represents the first deployment of the Adessia Stream platform in the U.K. and will deliver Britain's first mainline battery-electric train fleet, the company said.
said the fleet will be delivered from 2032 and is expected to enter service in 2034.
U.K. Prime Minister Burnham said the new trains would deliver "faster, more reliable journeys to the north and thousands of British jobs for the next generation."

title: Alstom signs €1.2B deal to build new battery-electric train fleet in Britain
